newsitem.title: USA: US Mint tender prompts wider zinc premium range.
newsitem.headline: US Mint tender prompts wider zinc premium range.

text.p: Premiums in Wednesday's offer of zinc to the U.S. Mint hit a surprising low at the bottom end of the range, traders said, but the overall market level is unlikely to change markedly.
The Mint received bids for 2,981 tonnes of special high grade metal (SHG) from four companies.

In light of the bids presented, the likely winners for 742 tonnes delivered to the La Salle location near Chicago will be Hochschild Partners at a premium of 5.0 cents a pound above LME cash zinc price.

For the Alltrista location in Tennessee, which comprises the balance of the metal, the winning bidders were likely to be Hochschild Partners and Ore & Chemical at premiums of 5.5 to 6.00 cents a pound.

Traders took comfort from the fact that the bulk of the metal went for 5.5 to 6.0 cents, in line with previous spot market premiums, but were disappointed with the 5.0 cent premium at La Salle despite the physical market still being fairly tight.
"I think we will see premiums remain at 5.5 to 6.0 cents in the market, and people will not go lower," a broker said.
Another dealer noted that the average premium in the tender was 5.6 cents a pound. "I don't think that's significantly different from what the market is right now," he said.
